sections.h2: What is Independence, KY like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Independence is a fast-growing suburb in the middle of Kenton County, and it is one of the few Kentucky cities where owners outnumber renters by more than four to one. Census QuickFacts reports an owner rate of 83.8% and a median household income of $102,361 for 2020 to 2024. A seller here is usually a family with equity, a home in good repair and a mortgage to pay off.

Growth explains the profile. The city counted 1,715 people in 1970 and 28,676 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate is 30,198, a rise of about 5% since 2020. Most of the housing is relatively young, which is why the sections below focus on permits, taxes and timing, not on old-house problems.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Independence housing?
sections.html:
The typical owner-occupied home in Independence is valued at $263,700, well above the other Kentucky cities in this batch of guides, and owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,666. Rent runs $1,250 at the median. Household size is the highest around, at 3.00 people per household.

  • Residents under 18: 27.9%; residents 65 and older: 10.7%.
  • Bachelor's degree or higher among adults 25 and up: 36.4%.
  • Residents living in the same house a year earlier: 92.9%.
  • Persons in poverty: 8.8%.
  • Mean commute: 27.2 minutes, which reflects work trips toward Cincinnati and Covington.

The 92.9% figure matters. Few households move in a given year, so well-kept listings get attention while a house with deferred repairs competes against homes that are move-in ready.

sections.h2: Where is Independence and how did it become a county seat?
sections.html:
Kenton County was formed in 1840 from parts of Campbell and Boone counties. A local farmer donated land in the center of the new county for its seat, and the name Independence honored locals' release from Campbell County. The legislature incorporated the town in 1842. Because most of the county's people lived along the Ohio River, Independence ended up sharing county seat status with Covington.

The city borders Elsmere, Erlanger, Covington and Ryland Heights, and its western edge follows the Boone County line near Florence. The original center is in the southeast along Madison Pike, and Kentucky Route 17, a four-lane divided road, runs just east of it, 11 miles to downtown Covington. Banklick Creek, a tributary of the Licking River, drains most of the city.

sections.h2: Which schools, parks and employers shape Independence buyers' choices?
sections.html:
Neighborhood schools named on the city's profile include Beechgrove Elementary, Kenton Elementary, Whites Tower Elementary, Twenhofel Middle School and Simon Kenton High School, along with St. Cecilia Catholic School, Community Christian Academy and Summit View Academy. Some parts of the city are zoned for Woodland Middle School and Scott High School instead, so confirm the attendance zone of the address you are selling.

  • Parks: Independence Park, Memorial Park, Pioneer Park, Doe Run Lake, Bowman Field, Lincoln Ridge Park, Mills Road Park, Richardson Road Park and Sterling Staggs Park.
  • Employers: Balluff, Cengage Learning, Krauss Maffei, Mazak and Rotek.
  • Library: a branch of the Kenton County Public Library.

Park access and school boundaries show up in buyers' questions more than almost anything else, so have both ready in your listing notes.

sections.h2: Do I need permits or inspections before I sell in Independence?
sections.html:
No permit is needed just to sell, but unfinished or unpermitted work can stall a closing. The city runs an online permit portal for joint building and zoning applications, covering new homes, additions, decks, sheds and basement finishes. Check that any past project on your house has a closed permit.

Documents the Independence residential permit portal asks for. Source: City of Independence, Building and Zoning Permit page.

Electrical and plumbing permits go through separate inspector offices, which the portal page lists. Zoning rules themselves are administered through Planning and Development Services of Kenton County, which publishes the Independence zoning ordinance online.

sections.h2: How do Kenton County property taxes and recording work for an Independence seller?
sections.html:
The Kenton County Sheriff collects current real estate bills through April 15 of each year. Bills paid after April 16 are handled by the County Clerk's real estate department. The Clerk keeps an Independence office at 5272 Madison Pike, open weekdays from 7:30 to 4:00, so you can record a deed or ask about a payoff without driving to Covington.

The County Clerk will not prepare documents or supply blank forms, so a title company or attorney drafts the deed. The deed tax under KRS 142.050 is 50 cents per $500, rounded up, charged to the grantor and collected before recording. At the $263,700 median, that works out to $264.00.

Questions about assessment or a homestead or disability exemption go to the Kenton County Property Valuation Administrator. The state's calendar sets January 1 as the assessment date and opens the roll for inspection for 13 days starting the first Monday in May; an appeal at the county clerk's office comes only after a conference with the PVA.

sections.h2: What if I need to sell an Independence house fast?
sections.html:
Move quickly on the items you control. Gather the permit history, the payoff letter from your lender and the most recent tax bill, then decide among the routes below.

  • List with an agent and price near recent neighborhood sales. Strong fit when the house is clean and updated.
  • Sell the house as-is for cash. Fits a job transfer, an estate or a house that needs a roof or a kitchen.
  • Wait and repair first. Worth it only if the work costs less than the price gap it closes.

With a median value above $260,000 in the city, a repair bill of even 5% is a five-figure number, so request itemized bids before choosing.

faqs.q: Do Independence homes sell faster than the Kentucky average?
faqs.a: The city has a tight owner market, with a 2.7% vacancy rate on the 2020 census and only 0.7% homeowner vacancy, so well-priced houses draw interest quickly. Speed still depends on price, condition and how the buyer pays, and I cannot promise a timeline.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax on an Independence house?
faqs.a: The Kenton County Sheriff collects the current bill through April 15. After April 16 the bill is delinquent and the Kenton County Clerk's real estate department handles it. Pay or credit any open amount at closing.

faqs.q: What is the Kentucky deed tax on an Independence sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays 50 cents for each $500 of value, rounded up, under KRS 142.050, collected by the clerk at recording. Foreclosure transfers are exempt. A $263,700 sale would owe $264.00.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to sell an Independence house with a finished basement?
faqs.a: Selling needs no permit, but a finished basement or deck built without one can cause questions at inspection or closing. The city's online portal lets you search permits by number or parcel, so check the history before listing.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for an Independence property?
faqs.a: At the Kenton County Clerk, which has an office at 5272 Madison Pike in Independence as well as one in Covington. Call the real estate and recording department at 859-392-1650 with questions.
